description: Black-Hole es un equipo de dos jóvenes dominicanas apasionadas por la ciencia y el espacio. Es nuestro primer Space Apps y, aunque ninguna programa, nos mueven la curiosidad y las ganas de aprender. Nuestras metas: aprender de la NASA y de otros equipos, crear una herramienta útil para la exploración de la Luna y Marte, y demostrar que desde República Dominicana se puede contribuir a la ciencia y al espacio.
summary: Synux is a web explorer that searches Earth by terrain type, not by place name. The user picks features such as volcanic flows, lake deposits, low rainfall or very cold nights. Synux checks a catalog of Earth sites and shows on a map which ones meet them, with their evidence and source. It then tells the user which place on Mars or the Moon that site tries to imitate, for example Olympus Mons, Hellas basin, Jezero or Hermite crater. A missing value appears as “No data” and never counts as met, so the tool is honest about what it does not know. Any country can add its own sites, and they appear in searches from their data alone. This lets students and scientists in our region discover what their own territory has in common with Mars and the Moon.
details:
What it does. The user ticks terrain criteria in a search bar, such as volcanic flows, lake deposits, low rainfall or very cold nights. Synux compares each site in the catalog using only the data in that site’s own card. The result for each criterion is “Met”, “Not met” or “No data”. Sites that meet everything come first, followed by partial matches. For the selected site, Synux works out which Mars or Moon target it resembles most (Olympus Mons, Hellas basin, Jezero, the north pole or Hermite crater) and shows how many of that target’s features it meets.

Data. We use daily 2025 data from NASA POWER (rainfall, humidity and temperature) and reference values for Mars and the Moon. Rock evidence comes from non-NASA sources (Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, USGS and a field study published in Geology), all cited in the references. Elevation, slope, ice and dry lakes (NASA Earthdata and Worldview) are marked as pending and are never counted as met.

Benefits and expected impact. It is an open tool for finding analog sites without knowing the famous names. Any country can add its own site with name, coordinates, evidence and source, and the new site appears in searches from its data alone. We added Lake Enriquillo, in the Dominican Republic, as a Caribbean candidate analog for Mars’ Hellas basin. Its elevation still needs to be confirmed. We hope local students and scientists can use and extend it.

Tools. HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single web page, with a hand-drawn SVG world map. No special hardware. We used Canva for the presentation.

Creativity. Instead of searching by place name, users search by the terrain features a base needs. The tool also shows its own data gaps openly, so a missing value never looks like a match.

What our team considered.

  • Missing evidence is not the same as a missing feature, so a site with no data is shown as “No data”, not “Not met”.
  • Earth cannot copy cosmic radiation, the real gravity or the very low pressure of Mars and the Moon.
  • NASA POWER grid cells are about 50 km wide, so a small site is averaged with its surroundings.
  • The criteria and thresholds for each Mars or Moon target are our own initial suggestions and are still under review.

Use of AI. An AI assistant (Claude, by Anthropic) helped write the code of the website, calculate the averages from the NASA POWER files, and draft and translate texts. The idea, the choice of sites and the criteria are the team’s own.
dataRefs: NASA POWER Data Access Viewer (daily 2025 point data)
NASA Planetary Data System, LRO Diviner (Hermite crater temperature)
projectRefs: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program (Haruj volcanic field evidence)
USGS geologic field-trip guide, Medicine Lake Volcano (Mammoth Crater basalt, Skull Cave)
Claude by Anthropic (AI assistant used for code, data averages and text)
